headline: High: Prefect’s broad egress plus caveman’s MCP/file surfaces create default data-leak and cascading-error risks; prompt-injection and compliance risks are lower but present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman can use MCP and reads/writes files like CLAUDE.md and project notes, while prefect can consume workflow metadata and call external APIs. A shared file or MCP bridge could let caveman-sourced content influence prefect workflows, but no direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF caveman content is passed into Prefect via a shared file, queue, or MCP server
IF Prefect treats workflow metadata from caveman as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Separate the agents onto distinct workspaces
Disable MCP bridging between the two agents
Add a manual review step before Prefect consumes caveman output
Prefix caveman outputs with non-executable delimiters
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on all shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, and prefect has broad network egress. If any of caveman’s files or logs are shared into Prefect, Prefect can transmit that content outward, creating a default exfiltration path. The pair lacks documented isolation, so the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF caveman files or logs are mounted into a Prefect task or flow
IF Prefect sends shared workspace contents to an external API
mitigations: Keep caveman and Prefect on separate directories
Block Prefect from reading caveman memory files and session logs
Restrict Prefect network egress to approved endpoints
Review shared artifacts before any upload
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: caveman supports multiple instances and writes local files, while Prefect is an orchestrator that can also mutate workflow state through API calls. Their write surfaces can overlap if they share a workspace or project repo, creating race conditions or conflicting edits. No locking or coordination primitive is documented, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or directory
IF Prefect and caveman modify the same workflow or note files without locking
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Run only one writer at a time
Use file locks for shared artifacts
Review git diffs before commit
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman produces content-writing outputs and project notes, and Prefect is an automation/orchestration system that can act on workflow metadata. If Prefect treats caveman output as authoritative, a mistaken or injected instruction can cascade into automated actions. Because the downstream action layer is broad and not guarded by default, high is appropriate.
conditions: IF Prefect uses caveman output as an input artifact without verification
IF a Prefect flow triggers actions based on caveman-generated text
mitigations: Require human approval before execution
Validate caveman output against a schema
Add a verification step in Prefect
Limit Prefect actions to dry-run mode
requires-engineering: implement signed, typed handoff artifacts

E_compliance.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while Prefect handles workflow metadata and has broad egress. That creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch if shared data includes regulated or sensitive content. No specific certification mismatch is documented, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in caveman files and then processed by Prefect
IF Prefect retention exceeds the operator’s policy for caveman artifacts
mitigations: Classify shared data before use
Avoid placing regulated data in shared files
Set short retention on Prefect artifacts
Document deletion/export handling
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls
